  PROBLEM: The routing treats every non-zero `git diff --quiet` exit as detected drift, so comparison errors such as exit 128 for an unavailable merge base can be routed as drift instead of stopping.
  WHY: On an “Any other base” path, the default check can error while the base check reports no drift, causing the procedure to record `claude_assets=stale` and continue under outdated guards.
- tests/test_claude_asset_sync_command.py:~210-378, ~380-429, ~480-481 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The executed-scenario tests do not cover `git diff --quiet` error exits, leaving the intended stop-on-error behavior unpinned.
  WHY: A regression that routes exit codes of 2 or greater as drift would pass the existing tests because none force the diff comparison to error.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:lines 186-189 (the new step 2 “Up to two checks” routing sentence: “Every check run exits 0 → nothing to do; any non-zero exit → step 3.”); mirror in `.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md` at the same hunk | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The routing sentence treats every non-zero `git diff --quiet` exit as detected drift, but exit 1 means differences were found and exit codes of 2 or greater indicate errors such as a missing merge base.
  WHY: An error on the default check can be recorded as `claude_assets=stale (base <base>)` when the base check exits 0, allowing the session to continue on the unsynced head.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:line 189 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The project-base verification sentence treats a non-zero exit as a stop, which is safe behavior and is not a defect.
  WHY: A non-zero exit on this verification already stops the session; no change is required.
